title: Falling cases: how many more to come?
hook: New cases drop 10% every day. How many more are still to come?

knows: the difference between daily new cases and the running total
doesNotKnow: that a falling daily count still adds to the total
that a slow fall makes a long, heavy tail

misconception: Once daily cases are falling, the outbreak is basically over.
objective: The learner can explain that a shrinking daily count is still a sum: 1,000 today falling 10% a day adds about 9,000 more, and a slower fall adds more.

claims.text: If 1,000 new cases today fall by 10% every day, the cases from tomorrow on are 900 + 810 + 729 + ..., which sums to 900 / 0.1 = 9,000.
claims.source: Geometric series a r / (1 - r) with a = 1,000, r = 0.9. Summed in node over 2,000 days: 9,000 (artifacts/scratch/w3life/check.mjs).

claims.text: On the stage at 10% a day, the total from tomorrow on is about 5,862 by day 10 and 8,999 by day 90.
claims.source: Partial sums 9,000 x (1 - 0.9^n): n = 10 gives 5,862, n = 90 gives 8,999. Same function (totalTo) draws the stage.

claims.text: At a 5% daily fall the tail sums to 19,000; at 30% it sums to about 2,333.
The model is a made-up outbreak whose daily fall never changes; real case curves do not fall this steadily.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; stated in the question, on the stage ('Toy: ... steady daily fall') and in the reveal.

recall.question: A toy outbreak has 500 new cases today, and each day has 20% fewer than the day before. Roughly how many more cases come from tomorrow on?
recall.why: The tail is 400 + 320 + 256 + ..., which sums to 400 / 0.2 = 2,000: a shrinking daily count still adds up.
